newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen remaining weak, testing downside.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen remaining weak, testing downside.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to remain weak and test the downside on Monday after Friday's sharp fall, traders said.
JGBs are likely to be sold if the yen falls further versus the dollar after the Group of Seven (G7) meeting, a trader for a city bank's securities unit.

"Since Friday there have been fears that (Japanese) interest rates may be raised in order to prevent a further fall in the yen versus the dollar. Such views could be strengthened if the yen continues to fall," the trader said.
The dollar rose after the release of the G7's joint communique, as the G7 failed specifically to mention yen weakness as a shared concern, foreign exchange dealers said.
In the joint communique the G7 stressed a need to avoid currency rates that spur trade imbalances, which indirectly referred to the yen and Japan's rising trade surplus, they said.
A bond trader for another city bank's securities unit said, however, that the dollar/yen rate's fluctuations so far may not be severe enough to have much effect on JGBs.
The dollar was quoted at 126.90/95 yen at 2305 GMT.

Traders said there will be interest in whether or not the Bank of Japan conducts an outright bond buying operation at 10.10 a.m. (0110 GMT), but they were divided on the possible effects on the market.
JGBs may be sold if the central bank decides not to conduct an outright bond buying operation, the second trader said.
The market has already factored in a decrease in the number of monthly outright bond buying operations by the BOJ, so the impact on JGBs is likely to be limited, the first trader said.
The market will also be watching industrial output data for March due at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), traders said.
